But its only core food section, 'Food' (5 items: 5pc Wings w/Fries, 3pc Tenders w/Fries, Bulgogi Fried Rice, Korean Bowl, Bulgogi Cheesesteak), carries an empty prices[] for every item despite paginatedMenuItems confirming itemCount:5 (genuinely present, not empty) -- these are priced only via modifier selection (3 have hasModifiers:true) and the modifier/option pricing isn't in this static payload, so no price is readable for any of them without a browser. The DRINKS (21 items, $3-$4) and PARTY TRAYS (20 items, bulk catering) menus ARE fully priced in the same payload, but both are adjuncts (drinks, catering trays) per house rules -- filing only those while the core fried-chicken items stay unpriced would misrepresent an adjunct-only capture as the menu, so blocking instead. Needs a browser to open the Food items' modifier modals and read the cheapest required option.

name: EL TORO GRILL TAQUERIA
notes: New platform not yet in the playbook: Smore Food (smorefood.com), a Next.js RSC storefront. The router's naive '$'-scan found nothing because the visible '$NN' tokens on the raw page are React Server Component reference ids ($1, $4, $L27, $undefined etc.), not prices -- the real catalog is a fully escaped JSON blob under the key rawMenus.menuCategories, reachable with a plain curl (no bot wall). Extracted by locating \"rawMenus\": in the raw HTML, balancing braces from its opening { (braces are literal, unescaped, only the quotes inside are backslash-escaped), then unescaping \" and \\u sequences before JSON.parse. 102 priced items across 19 sections (Breakfast Burritos/Plates, Seafood, Aguas Frescas, Sodas, Combo Plates, Plates, Quesadillas, Burritos, Chimichanga, Mulitas, Soft/Hard/Roll Tacos, Enchiladas, Sides, Tostas, Tostadas, Gorditas) -- taco-shop core sections all present. Address (4491 El Cajon Blvd) confirmed in the same payload. Markup test: raw prices land on conventional endings (.99/.49/.95 etc) at 98/102 with no division needed -- clean first-party pricing, no fee.
